title: The per-schema table list of the masked copy, the owner of the verifier across the 19 schemas and the PII extract contract are not stated
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 29, 31, 41 and 44); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 004 Masked data in SIT and UAT v1.md (sections 3, 11, 13 and 16)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 16 Test cases
description: RWB-TE-004 defines the masked copy against one recovery schema and a manifest with a row count per table. The target holds 19 schemas rwb_<name> with one login each and no cross-schema joins, and the Ownership Map resolves the tables the legacy story names to P1, P3 and P5, but no source states (a) which tables of the extract fill each of the 19 schemas, because the manifest is per table and not per owning service, so the loader's table-to-schema map cannot be read from any document; (b) who runs the masking verifier across the 19 schemas and how a partial failure in one schema is reported and rolled back, since the legacy story's verifier and staging swap are written for a single schema; and (c) the contract of the PII service extract, because the PII service is outside the source set, so the manifest fields, the delivery schedule and the extract file format are undefined. The integration run, its all-or-nothing rule and its verifier assertions cannot be specified from the sources without these three answers.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 29 (one ACE database, 19 Recovery schemas rwb_<service>, one login each, no cross-schema joins, views or foreign keys) and slide 41 (one schema, API, topic and queue per service); Ownership Map v1 resolves recovery_case, case_account, case_party to P3, interaction, party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext, valuation_ext and sys_fields to P1 and document_field to P5, and names no per-service list of the extract tables; RWB-TE-004 sections 3, 11, 13 and 16 describe one recovery schema, one recovery_next staging schema and a verifier on interaction and document_field only; no source document for the PII service or its extract is in the source set.
proposed: Publish, before the first SIT masked copy, the table-to-schema map of the extract (one row per table with its owning service schema), the verifier ownership and the partial-failure rule (one run, every is_personal column in every schema scanned before a single-step swap, any failure refuses the whole load and leaves the previous copy in every schema), and the PII service extract contract (manifest fields, file format and delivery window); the DB stories confirm the map for their own schema.

title: Chain-check scope across services, the ingest watermark and the Compliance route are not defined for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 008 Decision log hash chain check v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 14); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 20, 28, 42 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 15 and 16; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (JOB-13, JOB-14, EV-08, decision_log_entry, GET /decision-log, GET /admin/jobs, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun)
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 12.6 Schedules; 14 Validation and messages
description: Three points that the check needs are stated by no source. (a) No source says whether JOB-14 checks only the central ledger chain of rwb-decision or every service's local chain as well, and how a break that exists only in one service's local chain is reported. Arch v5 slide 28 makes each service write its local record in its own schema and hand it to rwb-decision through rwb.decision-record.v1, slide 14 gives rwb-decision the chain check at 02:00, and the Temporal and Drools design slide 16 lists chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash on the record, but the scope of the check over the 19 local chains is never named, and the legacy story verifies one log in one schema. (b) The legacy rule waits for JOB-13 to end and records its end time with a 04:00 latest start. In the target JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest into the ledger (Arch v5 slide 44; DP-17, RWB-E1-014 retired), so the check must wait for a producer watermark instead, and no source defines that watermark (consumer offset, business date or topic time), nor whether the 04:00 latest start still applies to it. (c) The legacy report MSG-P7-007 and the break report MSG-P7-008 with the incident go to the Compliance and PDPA officer group through the ACE notification path of the monolith. No source states how the incident and the report reach Compliance across services now that the check runs in rwb-decision, which service raises the incident, or where the JOB-14 run record lives when the job monitor is served by rwb-source-data.
evidence: RWB-TE-008 sections 3 (JOB-13 at 01:00 and the four parameters), 4 steps 2 and 6, 5 X1, X2 and X5, 7 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6 and AC8, 11 (decision_log_entry only), 12 (trigger, output, copyJobEndedAt, GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs), 13 and 14; Arch v5 slide 14 (P7 Schedules: rule promote 00:01, chain check 02:00; P7 writes the central decision ledger; FILE immutable storage: daily ledger seal), slide 20 (every service writes its own decision_record and publishes DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1, ledger in rwb-decision), slide 28 (steps 1 to 4: local record, chained, collected within 5 minutes, sealed daily; alerts for missing records; the chain checked every day), slide 42 row 08 (DecisionRecorded, producer all 19, topic rwb.decision-record.v1, consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting) and slide 44 (JOB-13 ingest is continuous (Kafka); JOB-14 Hash-chain check 02:00 rwb-decision Schedule; notes: overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window); Temporal and Drools design slide 11 (own schema: state + decision record; outbox to Kafka), slide 14 step 7 (RecordAndApply writes the decision record hash-linked to the previous record and the outbox row in one transaction; rwb-decision collects it within 5 minutes), slide 15 (governance and the ledger in rwb-decision) and slide 16 (the record fields incl. chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash, append-only and hash-chained, JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00); Ownership Map JOB-14 (P7, Temporal Schedule chain check, basis slide 44 and Temporal slide 16), JOB-13 (P7, no Temporal Schedule, continuous DecisionRecorded ingest), EV-08 (P7 owns the event type, the topic and the central ledger; every service writes its local record), table decision_log_entry (P7), api rows GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} (P7), GET /admin/jobs and POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (P1); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03, DP-10, DP-17 and section R5.4.
area: Decision log chain verification across services
proposed: Record the scope, the watermark and the route by assumption in ASM-B-ITG-W1-10-TE008-1 and ASM-B-ITG-W1-10-TE008-2: the Schedule lives in rwb-decision, checks the central ledger and every wave-1 local chain, waits for the ingest watermark with the 04:00 latest start, reports the first break per chain with MSG-P7-008 and raises one incident, and the run record is read through the P1 admin path; keep every legacy value, message and time unchanged (48,210 entries, chain_seq 30,005, 12,001 and 40,350, genesis hash of 64 zeros, 02:00, 04:00, 1,000 per batch, 20,000 entries, 37 appends, 10 million entries in 60 minutes) and confirm the three points at the wave-1 chain-check design review before the SIT run.

title: The call type between the client and rwb-agent, the run result after the 60 second budget and the guardrail check codes are not defined in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 13, 16, 41 and 42) and 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 013 Agent runtime client with fallback v1.md (sections 4, 5, 11 and 12)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: (a) The call type between the caller and the agent is not fixed. Architecture v5 slide 16 gives rwb-agent a Temporal workflow, AgentRunWorkflow, with 60 s and then the rule result, and slide 13 gives the P10 row REST calls only to P5 and P1; the legacy client called an in-process AgentOrchestrator and read agent runs through GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs. No source states which of the two the client uses in the target, so neither the client contract nor the workflow start can be written from a source. (b) No source states how the client gets the run result when AgentRunWorkflow completes after the 60 second budget: whether it reads the run, waits for AgentRunCompleted on rwb.agent.events.v1 or receives the result from the workflow, and what the applied result is in that case. (c) The guardrail check codes are not in the source set: the legacy story names "SCHEMA" as a check in one scenario and nothing lists the codes the guardrail checker of rwb-agent returns, so the fallback reason written to the decision record cannot be fixed from a source.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 16 rwb-agent IN: REST GET /agent-runs/{id} and GET/POST /agent-policies (admin); EVT DocumentStored and CaseCreated; TMP AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result, and Tool gateway read-only calls; slide 13 P10 row R to P5 and P1 only; slide 42 row 28 AgentRunCompleted on rwb.agent.events.v1 with consumers rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation; legacy RWB-TE-013 section 4 step 4 (in-process AgentOrchestrator.run with the step key and timeout_seconds) and section 12 (published interface AgentStepClient and GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs); no AsyncAPI document for rwb.agent.events.v1 and no guardrail code list in the source set.
proposed: Fix the client-to-agent call type and the post-budget read in the P10 contract at the wave-1 contract review: the client builds the rule result first, starts AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent through the P10 contract with the policy timeout, treats the expiry as TIMED_OUT with the rule result applied, and reads the run, its status and its fallback through GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs; publish the guardrail check code list with the policy schema so a fallback reason is always a code the agent returns.

title: TE006 outbox slice: the case-event mapping, the retry and dead-letter values, and the consumer list per event type
source: RWB-TE-006 sections 3, 4, 7 and 12; Arch v5 slides 11, 14, 16, 20, 42, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slides 11 and 14; Ownership Map (PLT library tables, P2 admin read, P3 case, P7 decision, JOB-10 and JOB-11)
description: (a) No source states how the legacy case events SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, RETRY_SUCCEEDED and RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED map onto the target signals and activities of rwb-case, or which service raises the RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY task once the outbox and task tables are per service. (b) The retry delays and the dead-letter alert route are not in the source set: the legacy 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes rest on DL11, which is not reproduced, while Arch v5 slide 11 gives the Kafka retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and a .dlt with an alert without naming the route. (c) The consumer list per event type across services is not defined: the legacy names win-dispatch, ledger and reporting-feed, Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 give partial consumer lists and no rwb-source-data subscription to the case events, and the two admin outbox paths are P2's although the library tables sit in every service schema.
evidence: RWB-TE-006 sections 3, 4, 7 and 12; Arch v5 slide 11 (retry topics 1 min, 10 min and 1 h then .dlt plus alert); slides 42 and 43 (event catalogue consumers); slide 44 (JOB-10 WIN notices 16:00, JOB-11 outbox relay every minute in every service); Ownership Map GET and POST /admin/outbox/deliveries owner P2, outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key owner PLT (ASM-A6-tables-8), JOB-11 PLT (ASM-A6-flows-9), JOB-10 P6 (ASM-A6-flows-8).
proposed: Run the wave-1 suite on the legacy values read as parameters and reference data: the three case effects as signals on CaseWorkflow in rwb-case, the task raised in rwb-case for the owner role in the consumer configuration, 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes in DEV, the retry topics and .dlt asserted as the topic contract, and the three consumers resolved to rwb-integration, rwb-source-data and rwb-reporting; approve the values before the story is Done.

title: The rule package of rwb-comms and of rwb-integration, the rule-model fetch path and its owner, and the message family of the refusal are not stated in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 27, 41, 43 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api rows and ASM-A6-api-3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 073 Rule authoring validation test scenarios approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (sections 12 and 14)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 AC3; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 14 Validation and messages
description: (a) Architecture v5 slide 43 row 30 names rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment as the consumers of RulePackageInForce, while the wave-1 services of this story are rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-integration and rwb-decision; no source states which rule package, by package code and version label, rwb-comms (P6) or rwb-integration (P2) owns or evaluates, so the upload, the load checks and the four-eyes approval cannot be driven for those two services from a source. (b) Architecture v5 slide 27 and Temporal and Drools design slide 15 name the model fetch as GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, but the Ownership Map and API Specification v4 hold no such path and no owner for it: both take the DMN model registry to rwb-decision and leave the fetch path itself unowned. (c) The legacy refusal keeps the identifier MSG-P3-027, whose P3 prefix names rwb-case, while the refusing service in the target is rwb-decision (P7); no source states the rwb-decision message catalogue, or the prefix and the path family under which a refused rule package load is returned.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 row 30 (RulePackageInForce, producer rwb-decision, topic rwb.decision.events.v1, consumers rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment, rwb-payment); Arch v5 slide 41 (wave 1 = P1 to P7, P9, P10); Arch v5 slide 27 and Temporal design slide 15 (GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, checksum verified, atomic swap, under 300 ms); ownership.json api rows GET /admin/rule-versions, POST /admin/rule-versions, POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve and POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/rollback carry the P7 ruling and ASM-A6-api-3 only, and no rule-model row exists; RWB-E1-073 section 14 fixes MSG-P3-027 for the refusal.
proposed: At the wave-1 contract review assign one package code and version label to rwb-comms and one to rwb-integration, add GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{versionLabel} to the Ownership Map and the API Specification under P7 rwb-decision with the checksum in its representation, and publish the refused load in the rwb-decision message catalogue keeping the legacy identifier MSG-P3-027 and its {check} values; until then the harness runs the three properties under the recorded assumptions.
